notes.text: Irish new lending has shifted decisively towards fixed rates: ECB data show the share of new house-purchase loans at a floating rate or with an initial rate fixation of up to one year fell from 31% in January 2025 to 6% in August 2026. New borrowers are therefore shielded from ECB moves for the length of their fixation, which slows pass-through to monthly repayments in both directions.

notes.text: Under the Central Bank of Ireland's mortgage measures, revised in October 2022, first-time buyers may borrow up to 4 times gross income and second and subsequent buyers up to 3.5 times, with a 10% minimum deposit for owner-occupiers and 30% for buy-to-let. Lenders may exceed the limits on 15% of owner-occupier and 10% of buy-to-let lending, which ties purchasing power to incomes rather than to credit conditions.

The Help to Buy scheme refunds first-time buyers of new or self-built homes the lesser of 10% of the price or four years of income tax and DIRT paid, with the cap raised to EUR 35,000 for purchases from 7 October 2026 to 31 December 2029. Demand-side grants of this kind support new-build prices and developer viability more than they improve affordability.

notes.text: Rent Pressure Zone rules were extended to every private tenancy in the State on 20 June 2025, capping annual increases at the lower of 2% or HICP inflation. From 1 March 2026 a national system keeps that cap but lets landlords reset to market rent at a new tenancy in specified cases, such as a first letting or a voluntary tenant departure, and at the end of a six-year tenancy cycle, while apartments commenced from 10 June 2025 may rise with CPI without the 2% ceiling to encourage rental supply.

notes.text: New dwelling completions reached 36,284 in 2025, up 20.4% on 2024 and the highest since the CSO series began in 2011, with apartments a third of the total. The recovery is concentrated in Dublin and the Mid-East, and output still trails the government's goal of at least 300,000 homes over 2025 to 2030.

notes.text: The CSO Residential Property Price Index is built from Revenue stamp duty returns matched to energy-rating and address data, and uses a rolling 12-month hedonic regression. It covers household market purchases only, excluding non-household, non-market and self-build transactions, is published monthly with separate quarterly indices for new and existing homes, and the latest three months are provisional.
